#### Slab Design  [Menus/Design/Concrete_Slab_Design/Slab_Design.htm]
Slab Design Slab Design Form: Slab Design Use the Slab Design form to display the design results. This form will be available only if the analysis and design has been executed. The various areas on this form include the following: Choose Display Type . Choose from the following options to specify the design basis and display type. The design basis can be strip based (i.e., design strips) or finite element based (i.e., slab objects) design. If tendons are present in the model, the Display Type can be Strength Reinforcing , Stress Reinforcing , Stress Check Transfer , Stress Check Normal and Stress Check Long Term, which allow numerical stress check values to be displayed at different stages. Strength Reinforcement is obtained from strength design. Stress Reinforcement is obtained from stress-based design. If tendon objects are present in the model, Enveloping Reinforcement is the larger of the Strength or Stress Reinforcement. If tendons are not present, the Enveloping Reinforcement is based on strength design. Design Basis drop-down list. Select either Finite Element Based or Strip Based as the basis for design. Display Type drop-down list. Select either Enveloping Flexural Reinforcement, Flexural Stress Check - Transfer, Flexural Stress Check - Normal , or Flexural Stress Check - Long Term . for the design information to be displayed depending upon the design basis selected. Impose Minimum Reinforcing check box. Check this check box to display the code mandated minimum reinforcing when it exceeds the required amount calculated by the program. This is applicable only when Enveloping Flexural Reinforcement is the Display Type. The following items may be available on the form when Strip Based is selected and the Display Type is set to either Enveloping Reinforcement, Strength Reinforcement , or Stress Reinforcement : Rebar Location Shown check boxes. Check the appropriate check boxes to show top or bottom rebar, or check both boxes to show both top and bottom rebar. Reinforcing Display Type options. Choose to display the rebar area or rebar of a specified size by selecting the appropriate option, and in the case of the rebar size, selecting the rebar number from the drop-down list. Reinforcing Diagram check boxes. Choose to display the reinforcing envelope diagram (and use the default or specify a scale factor) or display the reinforcing extent, or display both by checking the appropriate check boxes. Choose Strip Direction check boxes. Check the layer for which the design strip reinforcing should be displayed; the options may be selected alone or in any combination. Display Options check boxes. Check the Fill Diagram check box to show reinforcement using fill. Check the Show Values at Controlling Stations on Diagram check box to display rebar at the controlling station. Show Rebar Above Specified Value options. None option. When this object is selected, the program will show the required rebar. Typical Uniform Reinforcing Specified Below option. Select this option to refine the rebar display based on user input and provide input in the Typical Uniform Reinforcing area of the form. Specify the typical rebar based on size or area and select or enter values in the top and bottom drop-down lists or edit boxes, and then accept the default spacing values or specify other bar spacing by typing directly in the edit boxes. Reinforcing Specified in Slab Rebar Objects option. Select this option to base the rebar display on the definitions made when the rebar was drawn or added to the model. The following items may be available on the form when Strip Based is selected and the Display Type is set to either Flexural Stress Check - Transfer, Flexural Stress Check - Normal, or Flexural Stress Check Long Term: Stress Type Shown options. Choose to display either tensile or compressive stresses. Stress diagrams are displayed for the top and bottom fibers of the slab along the length of each design strip. Scaling edit box. #### Live Load Reduction Factors  [Menus/Design/Live_Load_Reduction/Live_Load_Reduction_Factors.htm]
Live Load Reduction Factors Live Load Reduction Factors Form: Live Load Reduction Factor Click the Design menu > Live Load Reduction Factors command to access the Live Load Reduction Factor form. Use the form to specify live load reduction preferences. Note that for live load to be reduced, it must be defined as a reducible type live load . Important Note: ETABS applies live load reduction to frame objects (and links) and wall-type shell objects only. It does not apply live load reduction to floor-type shell objects. Note: Live load reduction can be overwritten on an element-by-element basis in each of the design postprocessors (see the Design menu > { Steel Frame , Concrete Frame , Composite Beam , Composite Column , Steel Joist , Shear Wall } Design > View/Revise Overwrites commands) . The Live Load Reduction Factor form has the following areas: Live Load Reduction Method: Choose the formula or method, if any, to be used for live load reduction: No Live Load Reduction option. When this option is selected, no live load reduction is performed even if static load cases have been defined as reducible live load type load cases. Note: ETABS calculates the tributary area for a frame, shell or link element from the floor-type shell objects that load the element. If no floor-type shell object loads a particular element, the tributary area for that element is calculated as zero by ETABS . Tributary Area (Based on Design Code) option. ASCE7-95 option. When this option is selected, the influence area live load reduction method based on Section 4.8.1 of the ASCE 7-95 Standard is used. The basic formula is as follows: where, RLLF = The reduced live load factor for an element, unitless. The RLLF is multiplied times the unreduced live load to get the reduced live load. A I = Influence area for the element, ft 2 . The influence area for a column is taken as four times the tributary area. The influence area for a beam, brace or wall is taken as two times the tributary area. The RLLF factor is limited to Minimum Factor values (see bullet below). ASCE7-05 option - When this option is selected, the influence area live load reduction method based on Section 4.8.1 of the ASCE 7-05 Standard is used. The formula is the same as above (for ASCE 7-95), but where A I must be greater than 400 ft 2 . ASCE7-10 option - When this option is selected, the influence area live load reduction method based on Section 4.7.21 of the ASCE 7-10 Standard is used. The formula is the same as above (for ASCE 7-95), but where A I must be greater than 400 ft 2 . AS/NZS 1170.1-2002 option - When this option is selected, the live load reduction method based on Section 3.4.2 of the AS/NZS 1170.1:2002 Standard is used. The formula is the same as above (for ASCE 7-95), but where A I must be greater than 400 ft 2 . where, RLLF = The reduced live load factor for an element, unitless. The RLLF is multiplied times the unreduced live load to get the reduced live load. A = Sum of all area supported by the element, m 2 . The RLLF factor is limited to Minimum Factor values (see bullet below). Chinese GB 50009-2001 option When this option is selected, the live load reduction method based on Section 4.1.2 of the Chinese GB 50009-2001 Standard is used. The basic formula is as follows: The total stories beyond the design element LLRF 1 1.0 2 to 3 0.85 4 to 5 0.70 6 to 8 0.65 9 to 20 0.60 Over 20 0.55 where, RLLF = The reduced live load factor for an element, unitless. The RLLF is multiplied times the unreduced live load to get the reduced live load. The RLLF factor is limited to Minimum Factor values (see bullet below). Eurocode 1991:2002 option -When this option is selected, the influence area live load reduction method based on Section 6.3.1.2(11) of the Eurocode 1991:2002 Standard is used. The basic formula is as follows: where, RLLF = The reduced live load factor for an element, unitless. The RLLF is multiplied times the unreduced live load to get the reduced live load. n = Number of stories (> 2) above the loaded structural element. = 0.7 in accordance with EN 1990, Annex A1, Table A1.1. The RLLF factor is limited to Minimum Factor values (see bullet below). Indian IS 875-1987 option - When this option is selected, the live load reduction method based on Section 3.2.1 of the IS:875(part2) - 1987 Standard is used. The basic formula is as follows: Number of Floors (including Roof) to be carried by element under consideration LLRF 1 1.0 2 0.9 3 0.8 4 0.7 5 to 10 0.6 Over 10 0.5 where, RLLF = The reduced live load factor for an element, unitless. The RLLF is multiplied times the unreduced live load to get the reduced live load. The RLLF factor is limited to Minimum Factor values (see bullet below). Hong Kong COP 2001 option. When this option is selected, the live load reduction method based on Section 3.7.3.1 of the Hong Kong COP 2011 Standard is used. The basic formula is as follows: Number of Floors (including Roof) to be carried by element under consideration LLRF 1 1.0 2 0.95 3 0.90 4 0.85 5 0.80 6 0.75 7 0.70 8 0.65 Over 8 0.60 where, RLLF = The reduced live load factor for an element, unitless. The RLLF is multiplied times the unreduced live load to get the reduced live load. The RLLF factor is limited to Minimum Factor values (see bullet below). KBC 2009 option - When this option is selected, the influence area live load reduction method based on Section 0303.4.1 of the KBC 2009 Standard is used. The basic formula is as follows: where, RLLF = The reduced live load factor for an element, unitless. The RLLF is multiplied times the unreduced live load to get the reduced live load. A = Influence area for the element, m 2 . The influence area for a column is taken as four times the tributary area. The influence area for a beam, brace, or wall is taken as two times the tributary area. A must be greater than 36 m 2 . The RRLF factor is limited to Minimum Factor values (see bullet below). NBCC95 option - When this option is selected, the live load reduction method based on Section 4.1.6.9(3) of the NBCC 1995 Standard is used. The basic formula is as follows: where, RLLF = The reduced live load factor for an element, unitless. The RLLF is multiplied times the unreduced live load to get the reduced live load. B = Sum of all area supported by the element, m 2 . B must be greater than 20 m 2 . The RLLF factor is limited to Minimum Factor values (see bullet below). NBCC2005 option - When this option is selected, the live load reduction method based on Section 4.1.5.9(3) of the NBCC 2005 Standard is used. The basic formula is the same as NBCC95 above NBCC2010 option - When this option is selected, the live load reduction method based on Section 4.1.5.8(3) of the NBCC 2010 Standard is used. The basic formula is the same as NBCC95 above UBC-97 option - When this option is selected, the live load reduction method used is similar to that described in Section 1607.5 of the 1997 UBC. The basic formula used is: RLLF = 1 - 0.01 r ( A - A min ) where, RLLF = The reduced live load factor for an element, unitless. The RLLF is multiplied times the unreduced live load to get the reduced live load. r = Rate of live load reduction, 1/length 2 . The default value is 0.08 in 1/ft 2 units. A = Tributary area for the element or reaction, length 2 . If A does not exceed A min then no live load reduction is used. A min = User specified minimum tributary area for the element or reaction, length 2 . The default for this item is 150 ft 2 . The RLLF factor is limited to Minimum Factor values (see bullet below). User Parameters (per Section 1607.5, UBC 1997) - When this option is selected, the tributary area live load reduction method based on Section 1607.5 of the 1997 UBC is used. The basic formula is as follows: RLLF = 1 - 0.0008( A - 150) where, RLLF = The reduced live load factor for an element, unitless. The RLLF is multiplied times the unreduced live load to get the reduced live load. A = Tributary area for the element or reaction, length 2 . If A does not exceed 150 ft 2 , no live load reduction is used. The RLLF factor cannot be less than the Minimum Factor value , which is described below. Note that no check is performed to limit the RLLF based on Equation 7-2 in Section 1607.5 of the 1997 UBC. User Defined Curves (By Tributary Area) option. Select this option and click the Define button to access the Live Load Reduction Factor Curves form . Use that form to specify live load reduction factor curves by specifying reduction factors by tributary area. User Defined (By Stories Supported) option. Select this option and click the Define button to access the Live Load Reduction By Stories Supported form . Use that form to specify reduction factors depending on the number of stories supported by an element. Minimum Factor: The availability of the Single Story and Multiple Story edit boxes depends on the Method option selected. When available, use the edit boxes to specify the reduced live load factors (RLLF). One applies to elements receiving load from one story level only and the other applies to elements receiving load from more than one story level. If the Use default minimum factors check box is checked, ETABS will use default values provided for these minimum reduced live load factors. Uncheck this check box to access the Single Story and Multi Story edit boxes and specify those factors. The default values for the minimum reduced live load factors for the three different live load reduction methods are as follows: Tributary area method: 0.6 for elements with load from only one story level and 0.4 for elements with load from more than one story level. Influence area method: 0.5 for elements with load from only one story level and 0.4 for elements with load from more than one story level. User-defined method: 0.6 for elements with load from only one story level and 0.4 for elements with load from more than one story level. Important Note about Design Forces: In ETABS the live load is currently only reduced for design forces that are used in the ETABS design postprocessors. Live loads are not reduced in the basic analysis output even if the live load is specified as a reducible-type live load when the static load case is defined and live load reduction is enabled using this command. Thus when live load reduction is enabled, it is possible that live load forces will be different for the exact same item in the basic analysis output and the design output because the live load is only reduced in the design output. Again, in the analysis output, it is unreduced. Application: The Application area of the Live Load Reduction Factor form reinforces the above important note. The only application available in the area is Design Forces. It cannot be changed. If live load reduction is not to be applied to design forces in the design postprocessors, select the No Live Load Reduction option in the Method area of the form. Application to Columns: For columns, the live load reduction can be specified to apply to the axial load only (choose the Apply to Axial Load Only option) or to all force components (choose the Apply to All Forces/Components option). By default ETABS assumes only the axial load component of columns receives the specified live load reduction. This is useful when it is necessary to reduce the axial live load but not the moment caused by live load in the column. See Also Reinforcement Bar Sizes

#### Make Auto Select Section Null  [Menus/Design/Make_Auto_Select_Section_Null.htm]
Make Auto Select Section Null Make Auto Select Section Null The Design menu > { Steel, Concrete, Composite Beam, Composite Column, Steel Joist } Design > Make Auto Select Section Null command is used to remove auto select section lists from selected frame elements. Typically auto select lists should be removed from all frame elements near the end of the iterative design process so that the final design iteration is completed with actual frame sections assigned, not auto select sections. Setting the auto select section to null does not change the current design section for the frame element. Make Auto Select Section Null as follows: Select the Analyze menu > Run Analysis command to analyze the model. Select the Design menu > { Steel, Concrete, Composite Beam, Composite Column, Steel Joist } Design > Start Design/Check command to initiate design. Use the other commands to advance design to near completion. Select the elements whose auto select sections are to be made null. If no elements have been selected, this command will not be available. Often selecting all elements is the easiest approach. Click the Design menu > { Steel, Concrete, Composite Beam, Composite Column, Steel Joist } Design > Make Auto Select Section Null command to remove the auto select section list.

#### Overwrite Frame Design Procedure  [Menus/Design/Overwrite_Frame_Design_Procedure.htm]
Overwrite Frame Design Procedure Overwrite Frame Design Procedure Form: Overwrite Frame Design Procedure The Design menu > Overwrite Frame Design Procedure command can be used to change the design postprocessor for a frame element as follows. Select the frame objects to which the overwrites are to be applied. Click the Design menu > Overwrite Frame Design Procedure command to access the Overwrite Frame Design Procedure form. Choose from the available options. Depending on the frame section assignment made to the frame object, several of the options may not be available, as follows. A concrete frame element can be switched between the Concrete Frame Design and the No Design procedures. Assign a concrete frame element the No Design (Null) design procedure if you do not want it designed by the Concrete Frame Design postprocessor. A steel frame element can be switched between the Steel Frame Design , Composite Beam Design (if it qualifies), and the No Design design procedures. In this form a steel frame element qualifies for the Composite Beam Design procedure if it meets all of the following criteria. The frame type is Beam, that is, the frame object is horizontal. The frame element is oriented with its positive local 2-axis in the same direction as the positive global Z-axis (vertical upward). The frame element has I-section or channel section properties. Assign a steel frame element the No Design procedure if you do not want it designed by either the Steel Frame Design or the Composite Beam Design postprocessor. A composite column element can be switched to No Design . A steel joist element can be switched to No Design . Only beams that are assigned joist sections can be designed as steel joists. The joist sections can be selected from the built-in program joist section database, or they can be user defined. The user-defined sections can be specified using the Define menu > Frame Sections command and the Steel Joist option . No Design option. This option is available for all frame objects. It means that the frame object is not designed by any design postprocessor. These frame objects are given the Null design procedure. Default option. This option is available for all frame objects. It means that the frame object is to be given the default design procedure (postprocessor). The design procedure is not automatically updated as the model is modified. Thus if a frame object is drawn and the { Beam, Column, Brace } Information form for the frame is displayed by right clicking on it, the Design tab on the { Beam, Column, Brace } Information form may be Null or outdated. Display the current default design procedure for a frame object as follows: Click the Design menu and then click somewhere else to close the design menu. This automatically updates the design procedures. Right click on the frame object to display the { Beam, Column, Brace } Information form. The Design Procedure is displayed on the Design tab.

#### Point Brace Form  [Menus/Design/Point_Brace_Form.htm]
Point Brace Form Point Braces Form Define point braces by specifying a distance along the beam that locates the brace point, and then indicating whether the top, bottom, or both flanges are braced at that location. Specify the distance as an absolute (actual) distance or as a relative distance, both measured from the I-end of the beam. All distances are measured from the center of the support, not the physical end of the beam. A relative distance to a point is the absolute distance to that point divided by the length of the beam measured from the center-of-support to center-of-support. For example 0.25 would be 25% of the beam length from the I-end. Note : The Point Braces form also displays when a frame object is selected and the Design menu > {Steel Frame, Steel Joist} Design > Lateral Bracing command is used and the User Specified option is selected on the resulting Lateral Bracing form and the Specify Point Bracing button is clicked. Relative Distance from End-I and Absolute Distance from End-I options. Indicate whether the specified distances will be relative or absolute from the I-end of the beam by selecting the appropriate option. Braces - Click the Add button to begin specifying the point brace location and type. Location edit box. Input a distance form the end-I to locate the point brace. Brace Type drop-down list. Choose the brace type. Top means only the top flange is braced, Bottom means only the bottom flange is braced, and All means both flanges are braced at that point. Delete button. Click on a point brace specification and click this button to delete it. Sort button. Click this button to sort the point braces based on the location from the end-I of the selected beam. Click the OK button and to return to the Composite Beam Overwrites form. Note that the No. Point Braces item is automatically updated by ETABS to reflect the specified point braces. Access the Point Braces form as follows: Select a beam or beams. Select the Design menu > Composite Beam Design > View/Revise Overwrites command to access the Composite Beam Overwrites form. #### Set Lateral Displacement Targets  [Menus/Design/Set_Lateral_Displacement_Targets.htm]
Set Lateral Displacement Targets Set Lateral Displacement Targets Forms: Lateral Displacement Targets, Add Auto Calculated Lateral Displacement Targets For displacement optimization, ETABS predicts which members should be increased in size to control the displacements based on the energy per unit volume in the members. The members with more energy per unit volume are increased in size a larger percentage than those with smaller energies per unit volume. Some members with small energy per unit volume may be decreased in size if they are still acceptable for strength considerations. Assuming that appropriate steel frame, composite beam, or composite column auto select list assignments have been made, the displacement targets will be considered in steel frame design, composite beam design, or composite column design. Specify a displacement optimization specification as follows: Assign auto select sections to selected frames before running the analysis. Auto select lists must be assigned to the frame elements for the displacement optimization to work. When ETABS increases or decreases a section size, it uses the available sizes in the auto select list. If the appropriate sections are not included in the auto select lists, the displacement target may never be reached no matter how many times the analysis and design are run. Click the Design menu > Set Lateral Displacement Targets command to access the Lateral Displacement Targets form. Use the form to specify displacement targets for various load cases. Our intent is that the user picks a point, typically at the roof level of the building, and specifies a maximum displacement target (in any direction) for one or more load cases. Click the Add button to begin specifying the displacement data. Load Case drop-down list. Select the Load Case for which displacements are to be optimized. {Tower and} Story and Joint Label drop-down lists. Specify the location of the displacement by selecting the {tower and} story level and a joint ID. Max Displacement edit box. Specify the target displacement (in any direction) in the current length units for the specified load case. Delete button. If necessary, highlight the displacement optimization specification to be deleted. Click the Delete button. Sort button. Click this button to arrange the rows of data alphabetically by Load Case. Repeat Steps 1, 2 and 3 as needed. Rerun the analysis using the new section sizes to review the displacements. Displacement optimization is an iterative process that typically requires the analysis and design to be rerun multiple times. Note that it is not guaranteed that the displacement target will be reached using this option. Ignore Specified Target Displacements check box. Check this check box to exclude the displacements from a design iteration(s) without deleting them. Uncheck the check box to include displacements in design. Drift Ratio edit box, Base Story for Drift drop-down list, and Apply Auto Targets button. These options and button are enabled if a joint(s) is selected before the Design menu > Set Lateral Displacement Targets command is used. Drift Ratio edit box. The value for the drift ratio specified here is applied at the selected joint(s). Base Story for Drift drop-down list. Select the level of the structure where the displacement begins. Click the Apply Auto Targets button to have ETABS automatically calculate the maximum displacement for selected points based on the value specified in the Drift Ratio edit box and the story level selected in the Base Story for Drift drop-down list. See Also Steel Frame Design Procedure Set Time Period Targets

#### Set Time Period Targets  [Menus/Design/Set_Time_Period_Targets.htm]
Set Time Period Targets Set Time Period Targets Form: Time Period Targets For time period targets, specify a mode and a target period for that mode. Then, during design, ETABS automatically optimizes the structure to meet the target period using energy considerations. During the optimization process, members with large energy per unit volume are changed more than those with small energy per unit volume. Assuming that appropriate steel frame, concrete frame, composite beam, composite column, or steel joist auto select list assignments have been made, the time period targets will be considered in steel frame design, concrete frame design, composite beam design, composite column design, or steel joist design. Assign auto select sections to selected frames before running the analysis. Auto select section lists must be assigned to frame elements for the time period optimization to work. When ETABS increases or decreases a section size, it uses the available sizes in the auto select section list. If the appropriate sections are not included in the auto select lists, the displacement target may never be reached, no matter how many times the analysis and design are run. Click the Design menu > Set Time Period Targets command to access the Time Period Targets form. Click the Add button to specify the target data. Use the Mode Number drop-down list and Target Period display/edit box to specify the time period target. Ignore Specified Time Period Targets check box. Check this check box to exclude the time periods from a design iteration(s) without deleting them. Uncheck the check box to include time periods in design. Delete a Target. If necessary, highlight the target specification to be deleted. Click the Delete button. See Also Set Lateral Displacement Targets

#### Interactive Steel Design and Review_2023  [Menus/Design/Steel_Frame_Design/Interactive_Steel_Design_and_Review_2023.htm]
Interactive Steel Design and Review_2023 Interactive Steel Design and Review Forms: Interactive Steel Design and Review Interactive steel design is a feature that lets you review the design results for any member, select the best design from the various acceptable designs, and interactively change the design assumptions and immediately view the results. The Interactive Steel Design and Review form is available for the following design codes: AISC 360-16, AISC 360-22, CSA S16-19, CSA S16-24, EN 1993-1-1:2005/A1:2014. Access the Interactive Steel Design and Review Form Select the Analyze menu > Run Analysis command to analyze the model. Open the Steel Frame Design Preferences form and verify the selected design code is one of the codes listed above. . Select the Design menu > Steel Design > Start Design / Check command. Right click on a frame object to display the Interactive Steel Design and Review form. If design results are not current displayed, select the Design menu > Steel Frame Design > Interactive Design command and then right click a frame object. Use the form to inspect alternate designs for the frame object and select the preferred one Form Overview The form is divided into two sides. The controls on the left let you control the design while the controls on the right display information on the currently selected design, or let you access more detailed information. Left Side (Controls) The left side of the form includes: List of designs, labeled Acceptable Designs or Alternate Designs as may be the case Show Group Results toggle Show All Alternates toggle Auto Select List pull-down control Specify Section... button Group pull-down control Overwrites... button When the frame object being designed is assigned an auto select list , the list of designs shows the designs generated for the sections in the auto select list. When a frame object is instead assigned a specific section, the list is limited to the one design generated for that section. A design consists of a section, a camber, and several design checks that must be satisfied for the design to be acceptable. The controlling ratio displayed in this list is the largest of the ratios evaluated for all the design checks. When a design is selected from the list, the details of the design checks are shown in the Strength Checks and Deflection Checks areas on the right side of the form. If you click OK and the selected design differs from the initial beam design, you will be asked if you want to apply the selected design to the frame object. If you choose to do so and the frame object is part of a group which was considered in the design of the frame object , then ALL the frame objects in the design group will also be redesigned. If the frame object is not part of a design group, but there are stories similar to the story it is on and the Similar Stories mode or All Stories mode is active, then ALL the frame objects in the same location on similar stories, or on all stories depending on the mode, will also be redesigned. When the selected frame object is part of a group which was considered in the design of the frame object , a design is acceptable if it meets all the design criteria for all the frame objects in the group. However, the controlling ratio initially shown for each design is the controlling ratio computed when checking only the selected frame object and the design checks displayed on the right are the design checks done for the selected frame object. To look instead at the highest controlling ratios computed for each design when checking all the frame objects in the group, check the Show Group Results toggle. The design checks displayed on the right are now the design checks done for that critical frame object for which the highest controlling ratio was reached. The Show All Alternates toggle lets you view all the designs generated for the frame object, even those that arent acceptable. When you select Show All Alternates, the Acceptable Designs list is renamed Alternate Designs and designs that arent acceptable show up in red. Also, when none of the designs considered for the frame object is acceptable, the Show All Alternates toggle is initially checked, and all the designs are shown in red. The Auto Select List pull-down control lets you choose a different auto select list for the frame object, or no auto select list at all, in which case the section of the currently selected design will be assigned to the frame object. If no auto select list is assigned to the frame object, NONE is displayed. When the auto select list is changed, the design results are updated, and this may take a while if the frame object is part of a large design group. The Specify Section button displays the Select Sections form. Use the form to select a new section for assignment to the selected frame object. The selected section replaces any auto select list. If the selected frame object is part of a group which was considered in the design of the frame object, the Group pull-down lets you remove the frame object from that group, or put it back in. Click the Overwrites button to display the Steel Frame Design Overwrites {Code} form and review and revise design criteria for the selected frame object. Any changes made are committed to the model when you click the OK button in that form, even if you later cancel out of the Interactive Steel Design and Review form. Right Side (Information Display) The right side of the form includes the following for any selected steel frame object: Column, Beam , or Brace text box Story text box Last Analysis text box List of strength checks for select load combinations and locations along the frame object Plot of aselected strength check demand/capacity ratios along the length of the frame object The following items are only included if the frame object is a beam: List of deflection checks for select load combinations and locations along the frame object Plot of a select deflection check actual / allowable ratios along the length of the frame object. Critical radio button Scroll companion radio button Combos... button Pull down control for selecting a single design combo, or all of them Diagrams... button Report... button. The Column, Beam or Brace, and Story text boxes usually display the label of the selected frame object and the label of the story it is on. However, when the frame object selected is part of a group and Show Group Results is toggled on, these text boxes instead show the label associated with the critical frame object for which the highest controlling ratio was reached, and the label of the story that critical frame object is on. Last Analysis display box shows the name of the section that was used for this frame object in the last analysis, meaning the frame object forces have been computed for this section property. For the final design iteration, the selected design section property and the Last Analysis section property should be the same. If the two differ, you should re-run the analysis and then use the Steel Frame Design menu > Verify All Members Passed command and redesign any members that do not pass. The list of Strength Checks presents an overview of the strength of the selected design, with various strength checks reported in its rows. On each row, the first column lists the type of the check. The next two columns list the load combination and location on the frame object for which the check is being reported. The following two columns list the demand and capacity values computed while the last column lists the resulting demand/capacity ratio. All the ratios need to be less than 0.95 (or less than the Stress Ratio Limit set in the Steel Frame Design Preferences form) for the design to be acceptable. The strength check yielding the highest ratio is highlighted in bold. If the design is not acceptable due to one or more checks, those checks are shown in red. The plot below initially shows the values of the ratio along the frame object for the check yielding the highest ratio. However, if you click on a check in the list above, the plot of the ratio for that selected check gets displayed. Initially, the Critical radio button is selected. If you select the Scroll radio button, you can change the location for which strength and deflection checks are listed by clicking at that location on the strength check or deflection check plot. The list of Deflection Checks presents an overview of the serviceability of the selected design, with deflection checks for the various load conditions reported in its rows. On each row, the first column lists the type of load condition being checked. The next two columns list the load combination and location on the frame object for which the check is being reported. The following two columns list the anticipated maximum deflection and its acceptable limit, while the last column lists the ratios of the previous two deflections. The ratios all need to be less than 1 for the design to be acceptable. The check yielding the highest ratio is highlighted in bold. If the design is not acceptable due to one or more deflection checks, those checks are shown in red. The Combos button accesses the Design Load Combinations Selection form. Use that form to make temporary revisions to the design load combinations considered for the frame object and review the results. The changes you make are not saved when you exit the Interactive Steel Design and Review form, regardless of whether you click OK or Cancel to exit. The pull-down control next to the Combos button lets you design the frame object for a particular load combination, or for the selected steel frame design combinations. The Diagrams button displays the Design Diagrams form. Use the form to look at the applied loads, shear, moment, and deflection diagrams for the selected frame object. If the selected frame object is part of a steel design group and Show Group Results is selected, results for the critical frame object in the group are displayed. The Report button displays the Report Viewer and detailed calculations related to the design checks for the currently selected design. The form has buttons to move through the pages of the summary, to Zoom into the individual report pages, print the report, and save it as a Word document. See Also Steel Frame Design Procedure

#### SF - Interactive Steel Frame Design  [Menus/Design/Steel_Frame_Design/SF_Interactive_Steel_Frame_Design.htm]
SF - Interactive Steel Frame Design Interactive Design Form: Steel Stress Check Information (Code) Interactive steel frame design allows design results for any frame element to be reviewed, the design overwrites to be changed interactively, and the results to be viewed immediately. Access Interactive Steel Frame Design as follows: Select the Analyze menu > Run Analysis command to analyze the model. Select the Design menu > Steel Frame Design > Start Design/Check command. Right click on a steel frame element while the design results are displayed on it to access the Steel Stress Check Information (Code) form and enter the interactive design mode to interactively design the element. If design results are not currently displayed, click the Design menu > Steel Frame Design > Interactive Design command and then right click the steel frame element to enter the interactive design mode for that element. Use the various areas of the Steel Stress Check Information (Code) to review the design: Story display box. The story level associated with the frame element. Beam/Column/Brace display box. The label associated with a frame element that is a beam, column, or brace. Analysis Section display box. The section property that was used for this frame element in the last analysis. Thus the design forces are based on a frame element of this section property. For the final design iteration, the Analysis Section and the Design Section should be the same. Design Section display box. The current design section property. If the frame element is assigned an auto select list, the section displayed in this form initially defaults to the optimal section. If no auto select list has been assigned to the frame element, the element design is performed for the section property specified in this display box. It is important to note that subsequent analyses use the section property specified in this display box for the next analysis section for the frame element. Thus the forces and moments obtained in the next analysis are based on this section. Change the Design Section manually by clicking the Overwrites button and making the changes on the resulting form. Alternatively, select multiple frames and click the Design > Steel Frame Design > Change Design Section command to change all selected frame sections. Table Showing Stress or Deflection Details: The information provided in this table depends on which option is selected near the bottom of the form ( Strength option or Deflection option). Strength option. When the Strength option is selected near the bottom of the form, the table shows the stress ratios obtained for each design load combination at each output station along the frame element. Initially the worst stress ratio is highlighted. Following are the headings in the table. COMBO ID: The name of the design load combination considered. STATION LOC: The location of the station considered, measured from the i-end of the frame element. RATIO: The total PMM stress ratio for the element. When stress ratios are reported for this item, they are followed by (T) or (C). The (T) indicates that the axial component of the stress ratio is tension. The (C) indicates that the axial component of the stress ratio is compression. Note that typically the interaction formulas are different depending on whether the axial stress is tension or compression. AXL: The axial component of the PMM stress ratio. B-MAJ: The bending component of the PMM stress ratio for bending about the major axis. See Column Major Direction for a definition of the major axis. B-MIN: The bending component of the PMM stress ratio for bending about the minor axis. See Column Major Direction for a definition of the minor axis. MAJ SHR RATIO: The shear stress ratio for shear acting in the major direction of the frame element. See Column Major Direction for a definition of the major direction. MIN SHR RATIO: The shear stress ratio for shear acting in the minor direction of the frame element. See Column Major Direction for a definition of the minor direction. Deflection option. When this option is chosen near the bottom of the form, the table shows the deflection ratio for each design load combination at each output station along the frame element. Overwrites button. Click the Overwrites button to access the Steel Frame Overwrites form . Use that form to make revisions to the steel frame overwrites and then click the Details buttons to immediately view the new design results. Details button. Clicking the Details button displays the Report Viewer showing the design details for the selected design combination and station location. The form has buttons to move through the pages of the summary, to Zoom into the individual report pages, print the report, and save it to the Word compatible format. Envelope button. This button is available when the Deflection option near the bottom of the form is selected. Clicking this button displays the Report Viewer showing deflection envelope data for the selected design combination and station location .The form has buttons to move through the pages of the summary, to Zoom into the individual report pages, print the report, and save it to the Word compatible format. See Also Steel Frame Design Procedure

#### SF - View Revise Overwrites  [Menus/Design/Steel_Frame_Design/SF_View_Revise_Overwrites.htm]
SF - View Revise Overwrites View/Revise Overwrites Form: Steel Frame Design Overwrites for {Code} Steel frame design overwrites are basic properties that apply only to the beams to which they are specifically assigned. Default values are provided for all steel frame overwrite items. Thus, specifying overwrites is not necessary. However, at least review the default values for the overwrite items to make sure they are acceptable. Some of the default overwrite values are based on steel frame preferences. Thus, preferences should be defined before the overwrites are defined (and before designing or checking any steel frame members). When changes are made to overwrite items, the program applies the changes only to the elements to which they are specifically assigned; that is, to the elements that are selected when the overwrites are changed. Change an overwrite as follows: Select the frame element(s) to be specified overwrites. Click the Design menu > Steel Frame Design > View/Revise Overwrites command to access the Steel Frame Design Overwrites form. The steel frame overwrites are shown in a two-column spreadsheet. The left column in the spreadsheet contains the name of the overwrite item. The right column in the spreadsheet contains the overwrite value. Note: The Steel Frame Design Overwrites form also displays when the Overwrites button is clicked on the Steel Stress Check Information form . Click in any of the drop-down lists or edit boxes in the Value column to specify an overwrite value. The display area on the right-hand side of the form shows a short description of any item selected in the Item / Value columns. Further information about overwrites can be found in the code specific design manuals available from the Start Page or the Help menu > Documentation command. Set to Default Values area and All Items and Selected Items buttons. Click the All Items button at any time to reset all items to the program default. Click in the edit box or drop-down list in the Value column to select the item and then click the Selected Item button to restore that item to the program default. Reset to Previous Values area and All Items and Selected Items buttons. Click the All Items button at any time to reset all items to the previously specified values. Click in the edit box or drop-down list in the Value column to select the item and then click the Selected Item button to restore that item to the previously specified value. See Also Steel Frame Design Procedure

#### SJ - Interactive Steel Joist Design  [Menus/Design/Steel_Joist_Design/SJ_Interactive_Steel_Joist_Design.htm]
SJ - Interactive Steel Joist Design Interactive Design Forms: Interactive Design and Review, Select Sections, Steel Joist Overwrites, Design Load Combinations Selection, Design Diagrams at {Story Level, Beam Number}, Steel Joist Design {Code} Interactive steel joist design is a powerful feature that allows the user to review the design results for any steel joist and to interactively change the design assumptions and immediately view the results. The story level ID associated with the steel joist. Beam display box. The label associated with the steel joist. Design Group display box. Note: If a joist is redesigned as a result of a change made in the Interactive Steel Joist Design and Review form, the design group is ignored and only the single joist is considered. If you exit the form by clicking the Cancel button, these changes are considered temporary and are not permanently saved. Acceptable Sections: The Acceptable Sections list includes the Joist Section name, the Controlling Design Combination, the Stress Ratio Type (flexural, shear, live load deflection), Maximum Stress Ratio, and Unit Weight of the Joist (force/length). Note the following about the Acceptable Sections List If the joist is assigned an auto select list, many joist sections may be in the Acceptable Sections List. If necessary, use the scroll bar to scroll through the acceptable sections. The optimal section is initially highlighted in the list. If the joist is not assigned an auto select list, only one joist section is displayed in the Acceptable Sections List. It is the same section as is specified in the Current Design/Next Analysis edit box. At least one joist will be shown in the Acceptable Sections List, even if none of the joists considered are acceptable. In the case where no joists are acceptable, ETABS displays the section with the lowest ratio in a red font. Thus when you see a single joist displayed in the Acceptable Sections List in a red font, none of the sections considered were acceptable. Redefine, Temporary, and Show Details: Use the buttons in these portions of the form to change the design and immediately review the results. The optimal section is initially highlighted in the list. If the joist is not assigned an auto select list, only one joist section is displayed in the Acceptable Sections List. Click this button to access the Design Load Combinations Selection form . Use that form to make temporary revisions to the design load combinations considered for the steel joist and review the results using the Diagrams or Details buttons. This may be useful, for example, to view the results for one particular load combination. The changes made here to the considered design load combinations are temporary. #### Uniform Brace Form  [Menus/Design/Uniform_Brace_Form.htm]
Uniform Brace Form Uniform Brace Form Define uniform or continuous bracing by specifying a distance along the beam that locates the starting point of the continuous bracing, specifying a second (longer) distance along the beam that locates the ending point of the continuous bracing, and then indicating whether the top, bottom, or both flanges are continuously braced over this length. Specify the distances as absolute (actual) distances or as relative distances, both measured from the I-end of the beam. A relative distance to a point is the absolute distance to that point divided by the length of the beam measured from the center-of-support to center-of-support. For example, 0.25 would represent a point 25% of the beam length from the I-end. Note : The Uniform Brace form also displays when a frame object is selected and the Design menu > {Steel Frame, Steel Joist} Design > Lateral Bracing command is used and the User Specified option is selected on the resulting Lateral Bracing form and the Specify Uniform Bracing button is clicked. Relative Distance from End-I and Absolute Distance from End-I options. Indicate whether the specified distances will be relative or absolute from the I-end of the beam by selecting the appropriate option. Braces -- Click the Add button to begin specifying the location of the uniform braces. Start and End edit boxes. Input distances from the end-I to locate the starting point of the continuous bracing and a second (longer) distance along the beam to locate the ending point of the continuous bracing. Type drop-down list. Choose the brace type. Top means only the top flange is braced, Bottom means only the bottom flange is braced, and All means both flanges are braced at that point. Delete button. Click on a uniform brace specification and click this button to delete it. Sort button. Click this button to sort the uniform braces based on the start locations. Click the OK button and to return to the Composite Beam Overwrites form. Note that the No. Uniform Braces item is automatically updated by ETABS to reflect the specified uniform braces. Access the Uniform Braces form as follows: Select a beam or beams. Select the Design menu > Composite Beam Design > View/Revise Overwrites command to access the Composite Beam Overwrites form Click the Bracing ( C ) or Bracing tab. Select Bracing Specified from the Bracing Condition drop-down list. Double click the No. Uniform Braces cell. See Also Point Brace Form Steel Frame Design Manual (AISC 360-10) Composite Beam Design Manual: AISC 360-10

#### Verify All Members Passed  [Menus/Design/Verify_All_Members_Passed.htm]
Verify All Members Passed Verify All Members Passed When the Design menu > { Steel Frame, Concrete Frame, Composite Beam, Composite Column, Steel Connecion, Steel Joist } Design > Verify All Members Passed command is used, the program reports if structural elemennts passed the stress/capacity check. Click the Analyze menu > Run Analysis command to run an analysis. Click the Design menu > { Steel Frame, Concrete Frame, Composite Beam, Composite Column, Steel Connecion, Steel Joist } Design > Start Design command to run a design. Click the Design menu > { Steel Frame, Concrete Frame, Composite Beam, Composite Column, Steel Connecion, Steel Joist } Design > Verify All Members Passed command. ETABS will display a message indicating the outcome of the verification. If the message indicates a member(s) did not pass, repeat Step 3 until all members pass. Repeat Steps 1, 2 and 3 to verify the design and that all members pass. If necessary, repeat Steps 4a and 4b until all members pass.

#### Verify Analysis vs Design Section  [Menus/Design/Verify_Analysis_vs_Design_Section.htm]
Verify Analysis vs Design Section Verify Analysis vs Design Section The Design menu > {Steel Frame, Concrete Frame, Composite Beam, Steel Joist} Design > Verify Analysis vs Design Section command is useful for verifying that the last used analysis section and the current design section are the same for all { Steel Frame, Concrete Frame, Composite Beam, Steel Joist } elements in the model. This is important because when the iterative design process is complete, the last used analysis section property for a frame element and the current design section property for that frame element should be the same. If this is not the case, the frame element may not have been designed for the correct forces. Run what appears to be the final analysis and design iteration. Click the Design menu > {Steel Frame, Concrete Frame, Composite Beam, Steel Joist} Design > Verify Analysis vs Design Section command. It is not necessary to select any elements before using the Verify Analysis vs Design Section command. This command automatically checks all frame sections assigned the { Steel Frame, Concrete Frame, Composite Beam, Steel Joist } procedure. ETABS displays a message indicating how many frame elements with the { Steel Frame, Concrete Frame, Composite Beam, Steel Joist } design procedure have different analysis and design sections and then selects those frame elements, if instructed to do so. Sections Do Not Match. If the message indicates that the sections do not match, select No so that ETABS does not select the elements; repeat Steps 1 and 2 until the sections do match. When that occurs, design is complete. Sections Match. If the message indicates that the sections match, design is complete.

#### Bar Selection and Curtailment Rules - Column Stacks  [Menus/Detailing/Bar_Selection_and_Curtailment_Rules_-_Column_Stacks.htm]
Bar Selection and Curtailment Rules - Column Stacks Bar Selection and Curtailment Rules - Column Stacks Click the Detailing menu > Bar Selection and Curtailment Rule > Column Stack Bar Selection and Curtailment Rule command to display the Bar Selection and Curtailment rule form for columns. Use this form to set how reinforced concrete columns should be detailed and displayed in the detailing drawings. Important Note: It is recommended that these rules be set before detailing the model. If the detailing has already been run and changes to these rules are made, when detailing is re-run the program will prompt the user to (a) run the detailing and generate a new set of drawings or (b) synchronize the detailing and update only the items on the existing drawings that are affected by the detailing changes. Note: Bar Selection and Curtailment Rules can also be changed from within the Detailing Editor. Vertical Bar Layout Use the options on this area to specify what type of layout should be used fro these bars: The layout that's part of the section definition. An automatically selected bar layout based on the Rebar Selection Rules . Transverse Tie Layout Use the options on this area to specify what type of layout should be used fro these bars: The layout that's part of the section definition. An automatically selected bar layout to match the vertical bars and the Rebar Selection Rules . Enforce User Reinforcement Use these options to enter a user specified minimum and maximum reinforcement ratios for the column. Rebar Selection Rules This button will open the Rebar Selection Rules form which allows you to control the types of bars that are selected for your column. Tie Zones A, B and C refer to the bars in the column view shown in the Detailing Editor. Zones B and C typically are only present for Seismic cases. Bar Sizes: The Smallest Bar Size, Largest Bar Sizes , and the Preferred Bar Size can be specified for Vertical Bar Types as well as shear ties for Zones A, B and C. This is done by selecting the bar size from the drop-down list. Note: To add more bar sizes to the drop-down lists, go to Define menu > Section Properties > Reinforcing Bar Sizes. Bar Numbers and Spacing: Minimum and Maximum Number of Bars for the vertical bars can be specified by selecting from the drop-down list. Notes: When area of the specified Preferred Bar Size is insufficient during detailing and in such cases if selection of a higher bar size is desired rather than increasing Bar Number , the user must specify Maximum Number of Bars for the required Bar Type. Confinement (Non-Seismic) Click the Confinement button to open a form that allows you to specify what type of tie to use for the outer ( rectangular 90 or 135 degrees) or inner hoops (rectangular 90 or 135 degrees, vs L or U ties). When specifying internal ties, you must also specify the frequency of the internal ties. Confinement (Seismic) In addition to the same options for Outer Hoops and Internal ties as described in the Non-Seismic section above, you will also specify information about the length of the confinement zone. Bar Splicing This button will open the Bar Splices form where an how bars are to be spliced within the column stack. This includes the following: Splices at Every - This entry allows you to specify whether splices will occur at every story or at every other story. Splice Location - Use these setting to define whether the splices will occur at the floor location, the mid-height of the floor or such. Splice Location in Story - Use this to indicate where the column splice will occur within a given story (Floor Level or Mid-Height). Bar Splice Type - None, Lap Splice, Welded or Coupler. Splice and Embed Lengths - Specify the splice and embed lengths as a factor of the bar diameters. Min Splice Length - Specify the minimum length of a splice. Use Coupler instead of Splice - This checkbox will negate many of the entries above.

#### Rebar Detailing Options for Beams  [Menus/Detailing/Beam_Detailing_Preferences.htm]
Rebar Detailing Options for Beams Rebar Detailing Options for Beams Click the Detailing menu > Bar Selection and Curtailment Rule > Beam Bar Selection and Curtailment Rule command to display the Bar Selection and Curtailment rule form for beams. Use this form to set how reinforced concrete beams should be detailed and displayed in the detailing drawings. Important Note: It is recommended that these rules be set before detailing the model. If the detailing has already been run and changes to these rules are made, when detailing is re-run the program will prompt the user to (a) run the detailing and generate a new set of drawings or (b) synchronize the detailing and update only the items on the existing drawings that are affected by the detailing changes. Note: Bar Selection and Curtailment Rules can also be changed from within the Detailing Editor. Rebar Curtailment Options The different options provided for the curtailment of rebar are the following: Use Computed Reinforcement Only: When this option is selected, the program determines the bar location and length based solely on the reinforcement computed from analysis and design. Curtail 50% Bars: Check this box to curtail the reinforcement at the location where 50% of the bars are no longer required from the analysis and design results. Add Development Length: Check this box to add on development length to the bar locations calculated. Note: Using the Use Computed Reinforcement Only option may produce reinforcement layout quite different from the Use Computed Reinforcement and Curtailment Rules option in which curtailment rules are used together with computed reinforcement. This option should be used with caution and when manual checking and editing of reinforcement is expected. Use Curtailment Rules Only: Note: Using the Use Curtailment Rules Only option may produce reinforcement layout quite different from the Use Computed Reinforcement and Curtailment Rules option in which curtailment rules are used together with computed reinforcement. This option should be used with caution and when manual checking and editing of reinforcement is expected. Use Computed Reinforcement and Curtailment Rules: When this option is selected, the program computes the size and number of required bars at critical locations (top of support and mid span and so forth). It then checks the minimum and maximum number of bars and the like. A theoretical cut off location is determined for each bar. The curtailment location is then computed based on the specified rules and the governing bar location and length are selected. Check Development Length: When this box is checked the required development length/overlap length is calculated and added to the cut off location determined for each bar. Development Length Button: This button will open the Bar Development Rules form which allows you to specify information that affects a given bar's development length (coating, concrete type, etc) Curtailment Rules Button: This button will open the Beam Rebar Curtailment Rules form . Note: The rebar location and length determined by the program using these preferences can be modified using the Detailing menu > Show / Edit Beam Detailing command . Rebar Detail Options Use the options on this area to choose whether all bars will be detailed, or whether only bars above the typical bar layout should be detailed. Typical Bars: These options are available when the Detail Bars Above Typical Bars option has been selected. You may specify the size and number for the typical bars in the top and bottom of the beam. Only Where Required vs. Along Full Length: These options determine if the typical reinforcement is provided along the full length of the beam on only in the locations where reinforcement is required. Enforce User Minimum Reinforcement Use these options to enter a user specified minimum reinforcement for the top and bottom of the beam. Only Where Required vs. Along Full Length: These options determine if the minimum reinforcement is provided along the full length of the beam on only in the locations where reinforcement is required. Rebar Selection Rules This button will open the Rebar Selection Rules form which allows you to control the types of bars that are selected for your beam. Bar type A to G (or H) refer to the bars in the beam elevation for specific location and curtailment. These do not refer to the bar layers. Bar Sizes: The Smallest Bar Size, Largest Bar Sizes , and the Preferred Bar Size can be specified for Bar Types designated as A, B, C,,G by selecting the bar size from the drop-down list. Click the Note: Click to see Typical Concrete Beam Elevations link to view the Bar Type Definitions. Note: To add more bar sizes to the drop-down lists, go to Define menu > Section Properties > Reinforcing Bar Sizes. Bar Numbers and Spacing: Minimum and Maximum Number of Bars for each Longitudinal Bar Type can be specified by selecting from the drop-down list. The spacing factors for stirrups can be specified by directly entering the values into the text boxes. Also the anchorage type for stirrups can be selected from the drop-down list . Notes: When area of the specified Preferred Bar Size is insufficient during detailing and in such cases if selection of a higher bar size is desired rather than increasing Bar Number , the user must specify Maximum Number of Bars for the required Bar Type. Within the Rebar Selection Rules window you make click on the " Click to See Typical Beam Elevations " text at the bottom left of the form. Clicking this text will open up an elevation view that visually explains each zone and bar label from the Rebar Selection Rules form. Longitudinal Rebars in Section This button will open the Longitudinal Rebars Sections form which allows you to specify what size and spacing restrictions you wish to use for bar selection. This includes the following: Maximum / Minimum Bar Spacing - This can be specified as an absolute distance or as a ratio of the largest bar size. Minimum Numbers of Bars in each layer - This drop down allows you to specify the minimum number of bars in a layer. For beams this will often be set to 2, but can be set to any number between 0 and 30. Maximum Number of Layers - This drop down list allows you to choose the maximum number of layers. Spacing Between Layers - This must be specified as an absolute distance. It is a distance between the centers of the layers, NOT a clear distance between bars. Additional Bars in Beam Web - This covers the criteria for which additional longitudinal bars will be placed in the webs of deeper beams.

#### Beam Rebar Curtailment Rules  [Menus/Detailing/Beam_Rebar_Curtailment_Rules_Form.htm]
Beam Rebar Curtailment Rules Beam Rebar Curtailment Rules Form Access the Beam Rebar Curtailment Rules form as follows (click here) Click the Detailing menu > Bar Selection and Curtailment Rules > Beam Bar Selection and Curtailment Rules command to access the Bar Selection and Curtailment Rule form. Click the Cur tailment Rules... button. Use this form to specify how beam rebar will be curtailed. The Curtailment Rules are defined by specifying three types of information for top and bottom bars at different locations.The data that can be modified include the following: The shape of the end hooks to be used.Select Straight, 90 Deg bend or 180 Deg hook. The length of the curtailed bar as a proportion of the clear or center-to-center span length. The percentage of total reinforcement to be curtailed at the specified length. This scheme is similar to the rules specified in various design codes. Note: Detailing of beams can be completed using the Reinforcement Extent Based on Design Only option on the Beam Bar Selection and Curtailment Rule form, or the design can be completed as described in this topic. The changes described in the Curtailment Rules as explained here may not affect the final detailing of bars directly due to the consideration of computed bar cut-off locations, development and minimum bar length limits, and so on.

#### Customize Drawing Toolbar  [Menus/Detailing/Drawing_Manager/Customize_Drawing_Toolbar.htm]
Customize Drawing Toolbar Customize Drawing Toolbar Form: Customize Toolbars ETABS provides an icon or button for virtually every command. The default toolbars can be customized. Click the Options menu > Customize Toolbar command to access the Customize form which has the following tabs and buttons: Toolbars Tab: Shows all the available toolbars. Check the box next to a Toolbar to display that tool(s) or uncheck it to remove it from the CSiDetail Window. Standard: These toolbar icons control the standard functions such as New File, Open, Save, Undo, Redo, Refresh, and Unlock and Start Detailing. Edit: These toolbar icons control the standard editing functions such as cut, copy, paste, and delete. View: These toolbar icons control the standard functions for controlling the view including various zoom controls, pan, and rotate. The last icon allows you to show the model in the Detail Viewer. Details: These toolbar icons control the various functions for editing a view or detail within a drawing. These include edit view properties, edit view text , printing or exporting of the view / detail. Drawings: These toolbar icons control various functions controlling the drawings including drawing list, add drawing, delete drawing, rename, add delete or auto-arrange views, as well as printing or exporting for the drawings. Keyboard Tab: Click this tab to access the Customize Keyboard options: . Categories / Commands: The various commands available in the program are grouped into categories in the Categories display list. Use the Categories and Commands lists together to select the command for which you wish to see the current keyboard shortcut or for which you wish to create a new keyboard shortcut. Click on an item to highlight it and the specific commands within the category display in the Commands display list. If a keyboard shortcut is associated with a command, the name of the shortcut displays in the Current Keys display area. New Key / Current Key: If a keyboard shortcut is already associated with a command, the name of the shortcut displays in the Current Keys display area. Create / Change a Keyboard Shortcut as follows: 1. Highlight a command that has a shortcut assignment in the Commands display list. Note that the assigned shortcut keys will display in the Current Key display list. 2. Select the shortcut assignment in the Current Keys display list and click the Remove button. 3. Click in the New Key display box and then depress the new shortcut keys on the keyboard (e.g., the Ctrl key and an alpha character). The keys depressed will display in the New Key display box. 4. Click the Assign button. The new shortcut will now display in the Current Keys display list. Note: You may use the Reset button to return all shortcuts to their default assignments, or the Reset All button to return all shortcuts to their default assignments.

#### Drawing Manager  [Menus/Detailing/Drawing_Manager/Drawing_Manager.htm]
Drawing Manager Drawing Manager Form: Drawing Manager Click the Detailing menu > Drawing Management > Open Drawing Manager command to access the Drawing Management Component Selection form. This form gives you options about what type of detailing you want to include (or update) in the Drawing Manager form. Navigating the Drawing Manager Interface The image below shows the various areas of the Detailing editor windows with descriptions below describing the main features of each area. Main Window This window may be moved, resized, maximized, minimized, or closed using standard Windows operations. Refer to Windows help available on the Start menu for additional information about these items. Main Title Bar The main title bar includes the program and model names. The main title bar is highlighted when the program is in use. Move the main window by left clicking in the main title bar and holding down the mouse button as you drag the window around the computer screen. Menu Bar The menu bar contains the program's menus from which various commands can be selected to perform specific actions. The Edit, View, Detail, Drawings, and Options menus allow you access to various controls over the drawings, detailing and views. Edit & View menus This Edit menu contains standard copy, paste, cut and delete commands can be used on selected items in a drawing. This View menu contains standard commands for zooming and panning around the Drawing Manager window. This Help menu gives you access to the various options in the ETABS help system. Note: All the options under the Edit menu are applicable only for drawings and are activated when a Drawing Sheet or a View / Detail is selected. Details Concrete Display Preferences for Slabs , Beams , Columns and Walls . Steel Display Preferences for Beams and Columns . Concrete Component View Scales Steel Component View Scales Drawings This menu gives you access to the various options as described in the Drawing Menu topic. Options This menu gives you the ability to customize the Drawing Manager toolbar. Toolbars and Buttons Toolbars are made up of buttons. Buttons provide "single-click" access to commonly used commands. Holding the mouse pointer over a toolbar button for a few seconds without clicking or holding down any mouse buttons will display a short description of the button's function in a small text box. Detailing Explorer The detailing explorer displays the rebar details with the functionality to edit and view the rebar detailing. It has two main components namely Beam Rebar Details and Beam Views (For Beam) and Slab/Mats/Footing Rebar Details and Slab/Mat/Footing Views (for Slab/Mat/Footing). Items under Beam Rebar Details are useful for editing of rebars, view rebar quantities, edit labels etc. whereas items under Beam Views are for viewing purpose only. Similar definition is true for Slab/Mat/Footing Rebar Details and Slab/Mat/Footing Views. Also, there is an option to view the detailing output in 3D. This explorer allows easy access to details of slabs, mats, footings, and beams, including standard detailing results in graphical formats. Drawing View Window The detailing view window displays the selected component views. Multiple Detailing View Windows can also be added to view (2D or 3D) different Component Views side by side by clicking the arrow button on top right corner and clicking Add New Window button. If you select and right click on a specific view / detail within a Drawing, you will have the following options appear: Cut, Copy, Paste : These actions are the standard cut, copy and paste features, allowing you to manipulate the selected view. Edit View Properties : This brings up a window which allows you to change various items which control the way the view is displayed within the drawing. These include the caption, sub-caption, scale, line thickness, and the size of the view text and symbols. Edit View : This brings up the Edit View form which give you the ability to dimension the view, add text or otherwise customize how the view will appear in the drawing. Print View Export View Delete View Property Grid The Property Grid displays the general information about the project, story levels, and quantities of rebars. With this, the user can directly edit the rebar details such as Bar size and Spacing, Bar Length, Concrete Cover, Detailing Options, Section Details, User Label for Similar Rebars (in Slab Detailing), and Group Label for Beam Groups (in Beam Detailing). When the user selects any node from the tree, the user can modify the details of the respective object from Property Grid. For instance, the user can choose Top Bar from any one of the supports or spans and can modify the rebar details as per the requirement. Status Bar The status bar is located at the bottom left of the main window. Text describing the status of the program is displayed on the left side of the status bar. See Also Beam Bar Selection and Curtailment Rules Slab/Mat/Footing Bar Selection and Curtailment Rules

#### Edit Reinforcement Columns  [Menus/Detailing/Edit_Reinforcement/Edit_Reinforcement_Columns.html]
Edit Reinforcement Columns Edit Rebar > Columns Form: Edit Column Reinforcement Use the Detailing menu > Edit Reinforcement > Slabs/Mats command to access the Edit Slab/Mat Reinforcement form. Use the form to refine or modify the reinforcement layout that is automatically generated by the program based on the design results and the selected preferences. Select from the Slab/Mat drop-down list the slab or mat whose reinforcement is to be refined or modified. The upper window shows the reinforcement plan of the selected slab or mat object. Use the View Layer-A or View Layer-B button to select the layer that contains the target strip. Click on the plan in the upper window to select the strip with the reinforcement to be refined or modified. The toolbars along the tops of the windows include standard Zoom and Pan tools that can be used to optimize the display. The mouse wheel also can be used to adjust the view. Alternatively, use the drop-down list along the top of the lower window to select the strip or strip segment. When the design strip in the upper window is clicked or when the strip is selected from the drop-down list, the reinforcement calls of the selected rebar Strip/Segment display in the lower window. Click on a rebar call in the strip to display dimension handles. Click on a dimension handle, hold down the mouse button and drag the rebar to a new location. Click the handle at the end of the rebar to change its length. Use the edit box to specify a length that can be used to snap the location of bar ends while moving or resizing with the mouse. Click the Ast Profile button to access the Strip Reinforcement form, which displays a comparison between the required reinforcement and provided reinforcement in the selected strip/segment. The rebar call text can be edited to change the number of bars and bar size within the selected call. Note: Only valid combinations of number of bars and size written in proper format are accepted by the program. Typically, number bars, followed by valid bar size should be specified, as shown in the bar call. After completing the editing of the text or bar lengths, click anywhere in the lower window, other than the bar call components to accept the changes. Click the OK button to accept the changes made in various strips in the various slab/mat objects. The program will update the affected object views and drawings, including: Slab/Mat Reinforcement Plan Slab/Mat Sections Rebar table and schedule Reinforcement Profiles Button Action Changes to Selection Mode. Use this button to accept all changes in the current Strip/Segment and update the plan view. Shows the Design Strips in Layer A for selection and further editing. Shows the Design Strips in Layer B for selection and further editing. The Design Strip (or a segment of the Design Strip) can be selected from the available list. This selection also can be made by clicking on the desired Strip in the plan view. All segments in the Design Strip are listed individually for the purpose of reinforcement editing. Opens the Strip Reinforcement form to display a comparison between the required reinforcement and provided reinforcement in the current Strip/Segment. Select the distance used to snap the length and location of bar ends while moving or resizing using the mouse.
